slices.focus: Getting partial approval for a collections cleanup pilot with limited budget and two storage rooms
slices.summary: Hannah presents color-coded backlog counts, sample folders, and storage photos to win approval for a phased collections cleanup pilot — limited to two storage rooms with a tiny student-worker budget.
open_loops: Draft follow-up note naming the two rooms, first-phase goals, and what gets deferred
Build visual training packet (one-page side-by-side: complete vs incomplete folder examples)
Pick one manageable room and one harder room for comparison
Create quarantine pile/red folder for ambiguous records needing judgment
decisions: Hannah remains the Providence Museum of Art's registrar and won limited approval for a phased collections cleanup pilot

slices.focus: Addressing work-related jaw tension, headaches, and sleep disruption with doctor-recommended routines
slices.summary: After weeks of late nights writing procedures and training the first student worker, Hannah's doctor helps her recognize that chronic jaw pain, 3am waking, and deadline anxiety are a pattern needing active management — not signs she just needs to be tougher.
open_loops: Build three-anchor evening routine: shutdown note, fixed heat/stretching time, simple tension log
Define work boundaries in process terms (training blocks vs review windows) without personal-health disclosure
Draft boundary sentences ahead of time for when pressure comes
decisions: Hannah now uses stretching and heat therapy to keep deadline-related jaw tension and headaches from becoming constant.
